2026-07-20 China

China Day 10

Sebastian here!

Breakfast

With only the closing ceremony remaining, I was able to spend the morning with Rachel, so she came to my hotel in the morning to meet me for breakfast.

Botanical Garden

After that, we headed to the botanical garden. It was gorgeous!

Lunch

Quick stop for lunch before I had to head back for the last part of

Sebastian's afternoon

Closing Ceremony

Similar to the opening ceremony, we had wonderful performances. Kids from different ages performed dances from each continent. There was also a bit of opera and orchestra. We had our honorable mentions shown on the stage as well seeing all the medallists go to the stage to receive their medals (and a stuffed panda). Additionally, we congratulated 2 exceptional achievements: a student who got a perfect sccored for the second time in a row and a student topped the IMO Hall of Fame with 5 golds and 2 silvers in 7 participations.

Farewell Party

After the ceremony, we headed for dinner at the main cafeteria of Shanghai High School. There were a lot of games and activities (art & craft) where the students got a lot of souveniers and prizes. They also put enough of kiosks with dessets and snacks to have an entire 7-course dinner after dinner, lol.

A friend from Waterloo was here!

Wine :)

A bunch of the Latin American Leaders got together after the student's party to have some wine and conversations about our national math olympiads. It was great to hear how, even with limited resources, we are all trying to do the best for our students. With this I said goodbye to them and the IMO. Looking forward to the next one!

Rachel's afternoon

Tianshan Tea City

The Tianshan Tea City is an indoor market of tea shops. One of the tea shop owners, a lovely older lady, sat with me for over an hour explaining the different teas to me and let me sample each one. I had a great time and bought a few different teas to take home as souvenirs.

Xinzha Road

My greatgranparents were missionaries in China in the 1930s and 40s. The headquarters of the organization they were with were in Shanghai, but the buildings were surrender when the organization had to leave China in the 1950s. Before I left for China, my grandma was telling me the stories and showed me old photos. I was able to find the buildings - they are still standing!

A lesson learned

On my way back to the hotel, it started to rain. At first it was just a few drops, so I continued on to the hotel hoping to drop my bags before going out for dinner. I noticed all the locals starting to dash for cover in nearby shops, but since I didn't mind getting a little wet and I had a raincoat, I continued on to my hotel which was not far away.

Within minutes it was no longer just drops and became pouring. I was also having trouble with my maps and kept thinking I was just a block or two away from my hotel, so I continued on taking cover under roofs whenever possible. The rain kept getting worse and worse. Eventually I realized there was no point on continuing on, and decided to go into the nearest restaurant to get dinner before going back.

I saw what looked like a restaurant and entered only to realize it was a massage parlore. The workers there were super sweet and brought me paper towels and padded me dry. They gave me a cup of hot tea and offered me a massage. I waited there for a few minutes until there was a pause in the rain and then dashed back to my hotel. I arrived soaked from head to toe and decided that in the future when I see locals going for cover I should follow their lead.
